correctness.rationale: Three distinct columns violate two-row strength-three perfect hashing precisely when their grid edges form a three-edge path. A bipartite graph with no such path is a star forest; exhaustive maximality analysis yields spanning star forests plus exactly two complementary isolated-side cases. The standard labeled component exponential formula gives the spanning coefficients and associated Stirling partitions give isolated-side coefficients without overcounting. Every allowable cardinality is constructed. Two different executable checks agree at \(q=3,4,5\) and symbolic recurrence values \(q\leq8\); finite checks supplement an all-q proof.

Checked primary hash-family and star-forest literature gives definitions, bounds, maxima and related graph optimization, not a labeled all-q enumerator of every inclusion-maximal codebook. residual_risks: An older or unindexed enumeration of labeled maximal P4-free subgraphs of complete bipartite graphs could already imply the polynomial.

value.rationale: Greedy admissible column insertion can stop at an inclusion-maximal family, not necessarily a maximum one. The theorem determines, for every alphabet size \(q\geq3\), the complete labeled distribution of those possible terminal codebooks, all attainable sizes and the sharp minimum/maximum efficiency ratio tending to one half. This is more informative than known optimal-size bounds and is a natural full classification rather than an arbitrary slice.
